from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.play(FadeIn(guess_label), FadeIn(feedback_label))

        self.play(GrowFromCenter(star))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Calculating Entropy: Expected Information Gain", [
            "Entropy calculates the average information in guesses.",
            "Guessing splits possibilities into equal-sized buckets.",
            "High entropy choices resolve uncertainty fastest.",
            "We average information gain across all outcomes.",
            "Formula sums probability times surprise for all."
        ])
        
        # 1. Display Probability Distribution Histogram
        hist = VGroup(*[
            Rectangle(height=np.random.rand()*2+0.5, width=0.8, color="#FF00FF", fill_opacity=0.7)
            for _ in range(5)
        ]).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(hist, 'B2', 'E4')
        self.play(FadeIn(hist))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.wait(4)

        # 2. Overlay Entropy formula
        formula = MathTex(r"H(X) = \sum P(x)I(x)", color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'A3')
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(4)

        # 3. Highlight bars sequentially
        for bar in hist:
            self.play(bar.animate.set_color(YELLOW), run_time=0.5)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(4)

        # 4. Place Goal Anchor
        anchor = Dot(color=GREEN).scale(2)
        # Using a simple green circle as a terminal anchor
        target = VGroup(Circle(color=GREEN, radius=0.3), anchor)
        self.place_at_grid(target, 'F5')
        self.play(FadeIn(target))
        self.lecture[3].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(4)

        # 5. Pulse the anchor
        self.play(Indicate(target))
        self.lecture[4].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(4)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lines = [
            "Algorithms don't search for the secret word.",
            "They prioritize the most informative guess instead.",
            "The bot tames uncertainty using entropy metrics.",
            "Every outcome distribution is analyzed for gain.",
            "Entropy maximization is the key strategy here."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Strategy: Maximizing Entropy", lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show an 'Entropy Maximizer' slider in #00FF00.
        slider = Rectangle(width=2, height=0.3, color="#00FF00")
        thumb = Circle(radius=0.15, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=1)
        thumb.move_to(slider.get_left())
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(slider, thumb), 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.add(slider, thumb)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(4)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Visualize the slider moving to align with the 'Maximum Uncertainty' peak.
        self.play(thumb.animate.move_to(slider.get_center()), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(4)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display 'Entropy H(X)' graph changing as the guess distribution shifts.
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 2, 1], x_length=3, y_length=2, axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: -(x/4)*np.log2((x/4)+1e-5), color="#FFFF00")
        h_label = MathTex("H(X)", color="#FFFF00").scale(0.8)
        graph = VGroup(axes, curve, h_label)
        self.place_at_grid(graph, 'E4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.add(graph)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(4)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Place a 'Terminal Target' icon on the highest point of the entropy curve.
        target = Dot(color="#00FF00", radius=0.1)
        target_outline = Circle(radius=0.2, color="#00FF00")
        terminal_icon = VGroup(target, target_outline)
        terminal_icon.move_to(axes.c2p(2, 1.5))
        self.add(terminal_icon)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(4)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Highlight the final chosen guess distribution in bold yellow #FFFF00.
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFF00")
        # Final flourish
        self.play(Indicate(terminal_icon), run_time=2)
        self.wait(4)

outline.topic: Cracking the Code: Information Theory and Entropy in Wordle
outline.target_audience: University students (CS/Math background) or curious tech enthusiasts

sections.title: The Intuition: Why some guesses are 'better'
sections.content: Introduce the goal of Wordle as a search problem. Explain that a 'good' guess isn't just about matching letters, but about narrowing down the search space as quickly as possible.
sections.example: If you guess 'ARISE' and eliminate half the remaining dictionary, you've gained more 'information' than if you guess 'XYLYL' and eliminate almost nothing.

sections.title: Defining Information: The 'Surprise' Factor
sections.content: Define information content (Self-Information) as the negative log probability: I(x) = -log2(P(x)). Explain that rare events provide more information than common ones.
sections.example: Visual: A scale showing an 'Improbable Event' (a coin landing on its edge) creating a large spike in information versus a 'Common Event' (a coin landing on heads) creating a small flat line.

sections.title: Calculating Entropy: The Expected Information Gain
sections.content: Introduce Shannon Entropy as the average information (uncertainty) of a guess: H(X) = Σ p(x) log2(1/p(x)). A guess with high entropy splits the remaining word list into equal-sized buckets.
sections.example: Visual: A 'Bucket Analogy'. The word 'CRANE' acts as a sorting machine, distributing 2,300 words into various colored buckets based on the green/yellow/gray pattern result.

sections.title: The Strategy: Maximizing Entropy
sections.content: Show how an algorithm chooses a word not by looking for the secret word, but by looking for the word that produces the most 'informative' distribution of outcomes.
sections.example: An 'AI Detective' bot (modeled as a robotic fox) calculates entropy for every possible guess, selecting the one that 'tames' the uncertainty of the dictionary the fastest.

sections.title: Wrap-up: From Wordle to Reality
sections.content: Summarize how Information Theory principles apply to fields beyond games, such as medical diagnostics, data compression, and signal processing.
sections.example: Just as a detective eliminates suspects in a mystery, medical diagnostic trees use entropy to determine which test reduces the 'uncertainty' of a patient's condition most efficiently.
